A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C1INH is a gatekeeper for the brain.
C1INH deficiency induces a neuroinflammatory state, which is mediated by a peripheral vascular‐to‐brain axis.
the knockdown of circulating CINH induces neurovascular impairment via the KKS and the activation of glial and innate immune cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C1INH is an important regulator of the brain's immune system.
C1INH plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity of the BBB and brain function via the neurovascular unit, which is mediated by the kallikrin‐kinin system and the complement cascade.
C1INH plays an important role in the neurovascular unit and its manipulation may be therapeutically useful for neurovascular disorders.
